rules.text: Every change is a new version row; default queries return only the latest version per key.
Whether a field is required depends on the status of that version, never on a global rule.
A write whose session_id has a latest sessions row with status closed is refused with exit 3; --force and --as-gyb --force cannot override; the only way out is to reload a role.
Preconditions are checked at delivery, not at open; open only checks that the row describes itself.
Scan, number assignment and append happen inside one global lock loop/.lock; ql_tag and run_id are assigned inside the lock; batch is caller free text.
Sequence numbers start at 1; four digits is the minimum width, not a cap; sorting is numeric; a number once issued is never reissued.
Cross-ledger writes are ordered: first write the issue to get its id, then the handoff row that references it.
Every ledger has both write and query commands; queries are open to everyone.

gyb skips only who-can-call and the table's who-can-write; required fields, path existence and reference existence still apply; --force --reason records force_reason; a role using --force is refused with exit 3; --as-gyb --quote --force --reason counts as gyb.
